stemMd: Why does the author contrast a system of use with objects on a table?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To emphasize that operational context changes the environmental comparison.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To recommend evaluating products only by appearance.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To suggest return transport is impossible to measure.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To claim that material choice never matters.

options.label: E
options.textMd: To prove all reusable products are worse.

explanationMd: The contrast summarizes the move from one-off object comparison to life over repeated use, cleaning and transport. It shows why a product’s consequences depend on how it functions in a system, without dismissing material impacts.

distractorRationale.d: Manufacturing remains part of the calculation.
distractorRationale.b: The passage rejects a static surface comparison.
distractorRationale.e: Different operational patterns yield different results.
distractorRationale.c: The distributor begins tracking return routes.
